description: Peptide Patient's Guide v5 — Retrieval Quality Benchmark. Queries test NeuralMind's ability to find the right chapter/section for patient-facing questions about peptide therapy. Updated for Rye Walker's v5 edits (2026-09-14).

queries.question: What exactly is a peptide and how is it different from a protein?
gold_facts: A peptide is a chain of 2-50 amino acids
Proteins are chains of 50 or more amino acids
Peptides serve as signaling molecules (cellular messengers)
Insulin, oxytocin, and glucagon are examples of peptide hormones

queries.question: How does semaglutide work in the body?
gold_facts: Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist
It mimics the natural hormone GLP-1 produced in the gut after eating
It stimulates insulin secretion from the pancreas
It slows gastric emptying and reduces appetite signals from the brain

queries.question: What does FDA approval mean for a peptide?
gold_facts: FDA approval means the drug completed all three phases of clinical trials
Phase 1 tests safety, Phase 2 tests dosing, Phase 3 tests efficacy in thousands of patients
The drug received a New Drug Application (NDA) or Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) number
This is the highest standard of evidence a medication can achieve

queries.question: What is the difference between FDA approval and PCAC recommendation?
gold_facts: PCAC is an advisory body whose recommendations are non-binding to the FDA
PCAC voted to recommend 6 peptides for compounding in July 2026
Emideltide (DSIP) was rejected by PCAC
FDA retain final decision authority and has not yet acted on these recommendations

queries.question: How much weight loss can you expect from semaglutide?
gold_facts: Semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly achieved 14.9% mean weight loss at 68 weeks in STEP 1
In the SELECT trial, semaglutide reduced major adverse cardiovascular events by 20% vs placebo
Participants who stopped semaglutide regained roughly two-thirds of lost weight within a year

queries.question: What is retatrutide and how does it differ from semaglutide?
gold_facts: Retatrutide is a triple agonist targeting GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors
It is NOT yet FDA-approved as of mid-2026
Phase 3 trials are ongoing
It achieved up to 24.2% weight loss in Phase 2 trials at 48 weeks
Semaglutide targets only GLP-1; retatrutide targets three pathways

queries.question: What is BPC-157 and why is it controversial?
gold_facts: BPC-157 is NOT FDA-approved and is sold as a research chemical
It has no single established receptor in humans
Evidence is primarily from animal models with no human RCTs
Theoretical concern about blood vessel growth and cancer risk

queries.question: What is the black box warning on semaglutide about?
gold_facts: Semaglutide carries a black box warning for thyroid C-cell tumors
Rodent studies showed increased risk of these tumors
Human risk has not been established
Rodents have a higher density of GLP-1 receptors in their thyroid tissue than humans

queries.question: What is tirzepatide and how does it differ from semaglutide?
gold_facts: Tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist
Semaglutide is a single GLP-1 receptor agonist
Tirzepatide targets two gut hormones simultaneously
In a 2025 NEJM trial, tirzepatide demonstrated superior weight loss compared to semaglutide
Tirzepatide is approved as Mounjaro for diabetes and Zepbound for obesity

queries.question: Will there be oral peptide options in the future?
gold_facts: An oral form of semaglutide already exists using absorption enhancer technology
The absorption enhancer temporarily opens the intestinal lining so the peptide can slip through
Oral semaglutide has lower bioavailability than the injectable form
Researchers are exploring oral formulations for more peptides

queries.question: What are the risks of buying peptides from research chemical websites?
gold_facts: Research chemical sites label products 'Not for human consumption' to bypass FDA oversight
No guarantee of purity, sterility, or accurate dosing
Products may contain bacterial contamination, heavy metals, or completely different compounds
503A pharmacies at least operate under state board oversight

queries.question: Why do some peptide medications require refrigeration?
gold_facts: Peptides are inherently fragile molecules
Unlike small-molecule drugs like ibuprofen, peptides have bonds designed to be broken down
Exposure to heat or repeated freeze-thaw cycles can degrade peptides
A vial left in a hot car may contain biologically inert degraded fragments

queries.question: What should I ask my doctor before starting peptide therapy?
gold_facts: Ask if the peptide is FDA-approved for your specific condition or off-label
Ask what tier of clinical evidence supports it — Phase 1 or Phase 3
Ask what the documented long-term risks are and how they will be monitored
Ask about interactions with current medications
